cards.title: Manual Handling — The Basics
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- think T.I.L.E. before you lift
- lift and carry with good technique
- get help or an aid, and report a strain

cards.title: Everyone lifts
cards.body:
Lifting, carrying, pushing and pulling is part of nearly every job here: kegs, tables, mattresses, laundry, boxes of stock.

Done badly, it is one of the biggest causes of injury at work. Musculoskeletal injuries, such as bad backs and strained shoulders, make up around a third of workplace ill-health, and they can nag for years.

cards.title: Think T.I.L.E.
cards.body: Stop and think before you lift anything.

items.title: Task
items.text: What am I moving, and where to?

items.title: Individual
items.text: Can I do this, or do I need help?

items.title: Load
items.text: How heavy and awkward is it?

items.title: Environment
items.text: Is the floor clear and dry, and my route clear?

cards.title: Do not be a hero
cards.body: If a load is too heavy or awkward, get someone to help, or use a trolley, sack barrow or other aid.

items.title: Use an aid
items.text: Trolley, sack barrow or other aid

items.title: Get help
items.text: Ask someone to lift with you

items.title: Never
items.text: Try to be a hero alone

cards.title: The golden rules
cards.body: Plan your route first. Stand close to the load with your feet slightly apart. Get a secure grip, then lift smoothly using the power in your legs.

left.title: Do
items: Keep the load close to your body

right.title: Do not
items: Hold the load away from you

cards.title: Carrying and setting down
cards.body:
Do not carry so much that you cannot see where you are going.

Set loads down carefully, watching your fingers and toes. Push rather than pull where you can.

> If you feel a strain or twinge, stop straight away and report it.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Think T.I.L.E. before every lift
- Bend your knees, keep your back straight, keep the load close
- Move your feet to turn; never twist
- Too heavy or awkward: get help or use an aid
- Stop and report any strain or twinge

cards.q: What do the letters T.I.L.E. stand for?
cards.why: T.I.L.E. is Task, Individual, Load, Environment, the four things to think about before you lift.

cards.q: When lifting, you should bend your:
cards.why: Bend your knees rather than your back, and lift using the power in your legs.

cards.q: You should keep the load close to your body.
cards.why: Keeping the load close to your body is one of the golden rules.

cards.q: It is fine to twist your body while lifting a load.
cards.why: Never twist while carrying. Move your feet to turn instead.

cards.q: If a load is too heavy or awkward, what should you do?
options: Get help or use a trolley or sack barrow
Lift it slowly so it feels lighter
Drag it along the floor to save lifting
Leave it where it is for the next shift
cards.why: Do not try to be a hero: get someone to help, or use a trolley, sack barrow or other aid.

cards.q: To turn while carrying a load you should:
cards.why: Move your feet to turn instead of twisting.

cards.q: It is fine to carry so much that you cannot see over the load.
cards.why: Do not carry so much that you cannot see where you are going.

cards.q: Which of these is a lifting aid that can help with a heavy load?
options: A step stool from the store
cards.why: A trolley or sack barrow takes the weight so you do not have to carry it.

cards.q: You should push rather than pull where you can.
cards.why: Push rather than pull where you can; it is easier on your body.

cards.q: If you feel a strain while lifting, you should:
options: Push through it and finish the job
Lift faster to get it over with
Rest it until the end of the shift
cards.why: Stop straight away and report it.
